title: Consolidated consumption scenarios and commercial packaging
author: Marina Alvarez
content:
Summary:
This document consolidates representative customer consumption scenarios and maps them to commercial packaging options for Redwood Inference. It blends product requirements, pricing archetypes, onboarding flows, and launch checklist items into a single reference intended for Product, GTM, and Sales Engineering. The goal is to provide clear mappings from real-world workload patterns to recommended tiers, credit models, and migration steps so that customers receive predictable economics and predictable SLOs.

Audience:
- Product managers and pricing owners
- Sales engineering and solutions architects
- GTM and account teams
- Finance and revenue operations

Scope and aims:
- Define 6 canonical consumption scenarios derived from field patterns.
- Map each scenario to 2–3 commercial packaging options (hosted, dedicated commit, hybrid credits).
- Provide sample pricing bands and per-unit economics for standard instance sizes.
- Specify PRD-level requirements for telemetry, billing metering hooks, and onboarding automation.
- Deliver a rollout and migration plan for early adopter customers.

Canonical consumption scenarios (high-level):
1) Intermittent query bursts (startups, low-traffic prototypes)
   - Characteristics: <100QPS spikes of short chat interactions, heavy short-lived concurrency, token distribution skewed toward short prompts (<128 tokens).
   - Primary concerns: cost predictability, self-serve onboarding friction, instant throttle/guardrails.

2) Steady high-throughput batch generation (analytics, nightly jobs)
   - Characteristics: large daily token volume, predictable windows for heavy load, tolerant of higher latency but wants low per-token cost.
   - Primary concerns: reserved capacity efficiency, batch/throughput discounts, offline prefetching.

3) Low-latency conversational product (consumer-facing chat)
   - Characteristics: strict p95 latency targets (<150ms for token stream), sustained medium QPS, high retention of KV cache across sessions.
   - Primary concerns: dedicated SLOs, KV cache affinity, failover behavior, stream reliability.

4) Regulated/private data (healthcare/finance)
   - Characteristics: private deployment or VPC, audit logs, region-bound residency, strict encryption and KMS controls.
   - Primary concerns: on-prem/private pricing, support SLAs, audit and compliance add-ons.

5) Embeddings-heavy similarity/retrieval ops
   - Characteristics: high volume of small embedding requests, long-term storage TTL for vectors, occasional re-index windows.
   - Primary concerns: per-embedding unit pricing, retention tiering, hybrid cache near-data.

6) Mixed-fidelity pipelines (multimodel pipelines)
   - Characteristics: orchestrated flows that use low-cost models for retrieval/generation and high-fidelity models for finalization.
   - Primary concerns: routing rules, cross-model pass-through costs, fidelity budget caps.

Packaging options and mapping matrix:
- Packaging model A: Self-serve hosted credits
  - Description: pay-as-you-go token & embedding credits, immediate signup, conservative quotas.
  - Fit: Intermittent bursts, small embedding workloads, prototypes.

- Packaging model B: Reserved commit (Dedicated Lite / Dedicated Pro)
  - Description: monthly/annual GPU capacity commitments with discounted per-token rates and priority routing.
  - Fit: Batch generation, low-latency conversational products, high consistent throughput.

- Packaging model C: Hybrid credits + SLO overlay
  - Description: mixture of on-demand credits and reserved pools with explicit SLOs and overflow pricing for bursts.
  - Fit: Mixed-fidelity pipelines, customers requiring elasticity but predictable economics.

- Packaging model D: Private deployment license + support
  - Description: Private control plane or VPC deployment, platform fee, per-node pricing, optional on-prem bundle.
  - Fit: Regulated industries and enterprise customers requiring isolation.

Sample commercial mapping (short):
- Intermittent query bursts -> Model A (Self-serve credits) OR Model C for growth path
- Steady high-throughput batch -> Model B (Reserved commit) with batch-optimized rate cards
- Low-latency conversational -> Model B (Dedicated Pro) + SLO add-on
- Regulated/private data -> Model D (Private) + Compliance package pricing
- Embeddings-heavy -> Model A (for small users) or Model B with embeddings unit discounts
- Mixed-fidelity pipelines -> Model C (Hybrid) with explicit routing credit rules

Pricing examples and economic bands (illustrative only):
| Package | Typical commit | Effective per-1k-token rate* | Embedding unit | Notes |
|---------|----------------|-----------------------------|----------------|-------|
| Self-serve credits | No commit | $0.035 | $0.003 per embed | High elasticity, list pricing
| Dedicated Lite | $10k/mo | $0.018 | $0.0025 | Lower latency tier, limited concurrency guarantees
| Dedicated Pro | $50k/mo | $0.010 | $0.002 | SLO-backed, priority routing, KV affinity
| Hybrid SLO overlay | $25k/mo + credits | $0.012 (for committed) | $0.0022 | Burst overflow at on-demand rates
* Effective per-1k-token rates are examples for standard sequence length distributions; final econs depend on quantization and batching.

PRD-level requirements (high priority):
- Metering: Emit per-request metering events including model_id, route_id, token_in, token_out, fidelity_flag, and routing_decision. Owner: Product/Telemetry. Target: instrumented in initial GA.
- Billing hooks: Billing buffer that consumes metering events with 10s SLA to ledger. Support both eventstream and batch ingest. Owner: Finance + Platform.
- SLO metadata: Every provisioning option must accept SLO profile (latency p95, availability) and be surfaced in the console. Owner: Product/Console.
- Onboarding automation: Guided onboarding flow that recommends packaging based on a short workload questionnaire and a 7-day trial of recommended tier. Owner: Growth/Product.
- Migration path: Provide an automated migration tool to move tenants from hosted credits to a dedicated commit, transferring active routing policies and KV cache affinity where possible. Owner: Platform/Eng-Private-Deployments.

Implementation checklist (table):
- Telemetry schema v2 published and backward compatible with v1. Owner: eng-platform. ETA: 2028-04-15.
- Billing ledger adapter for hybrid credits implemented. Owner: finance-legal + eng-infra. ETA: 2028-05-01.
- Console UI: packaging chooser + migration wizard. Owner: eng-developer-experience. ETA: 2028-05-15.
- Sales enablement: case studies and pricing cards produced. Owner: go-to-market. ETA: 2028-05-22.

Sample onboarding migration flow (numbered steps):
1. Sales selects customer archetype and proposes target package in Deal Desk.
2. Customer starts a 7-day trial of recommended tier (prefilled config).
3. During trial, telemetry capture runs a 72-hour workload analysis (token shapes, concurrency patterns).
4. System recommends either self-serve conversion, commit proposal, or private deployment; automated cost-savings calc is surfaced.
5. If commit chosen, execute reservation contract and schedule capacity provisioning; dry-run migration copies KV metadata and warms caches.
6. Post-migration, run verification tests against p95 latency and cost burn targets for 72 hours; if fails, trigger rollback plan.

Rollout roadmap (quarterly milestones):
- Q2 2028: finalize pricing bands and telemetry schema; pilot 3 customers across scenarios 1, 2, and 5.
- Q3 2028: deliver migration wizard and reserved-commit billing adapter; expand pilot to conversational customers.
- Q4 2028: launch public GTM materials, integrate with console billing UI, and release SLO add-on.

Risk assessment and mitigations:
- Risk: Overly complex packaging confuses customers. Mitigation: Limit to 3 primary flows and 2 growth paths; surface an automated recommendation.
- Risk: Metering inaccuracies affect revenue. Mitigation: Parallel shadow billing during pilot and reconciliation tools before GA.
- Risk: Performance regressions on committed capacity. Mitigation: Clear SLAs, canary allocations, and automatic fallback to compatible variants.

Monitoring and KPIs (examples):
- Adoption conversion rate: trial -> commit within 30 days (target 12%).
- Average effective per-1k-token realized against list (target within 10% of modeled band).
- Migration success rate (post-verification) >95%.
- Billing reconciliation drift <0.5% per month.

Open questions for leadership:
- Should we offer a fixed-duration low-cost pilot SKU for regulated customers to reduce procurement friction?
- How aggressive should per-embed discounts be vs. per-token discounts to avoid arbitrage in multimodel flows?
- What telemetry retention window is acceptable for finance reconciliation without adding undue storage cost?

Appendix A — example telemetry event (JSON):
{
  "timestamp": "2028-03-01T14:12:05Z",
  "tenant_id": "acct-12345",
  "model_id": "rwd-gpt-large-quant",
  "route_id": "conv-usa-prod",
  "tokens_in": 34,
  "tokens_out": 112,
  "fidelity": "medium",
  "routing_decision": "dedicated-pro"
}

Appendix B — sample API call to estimate cost (curl):
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/estimate" -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{
  "prototype_profile": "conversational-low-latency",
  "avg_tokens_in": 20,
  "avg_tokens_out": 80,
  "qps": 40
}'

Appendix C — decision log (short):
- 2028-02-14: agreed not to introduce unlimited-burst tiers for Dedicated Pro to protect capacity economics.
- 2028-02-28: approved telemetry v2 fields for billing and SLO classification.
